item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 241742
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM HST Mon Aug 24 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Pearl and Hermes
Atoll, on Tropical Depression Moke, located several hundred miles
south-southwest of Honolulu, Hawaii, and on Tropical Storm Iselle,
located several hundred miles west-southwest of the southern tip of
the Baja California Peninsula.

Western East Pacific:
A trough of low pressure located well to the east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands is producing some disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. Some slow development of this system is possible
over the next several days while it drifts north-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Hagen

...LALA MAINTAINING ITS INTENSITY FOR NOW...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM HST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...33.7N 175.4W
ABOUT 430 MI...690 KM N OF PEARL AND HERMES ATOLL
ABOUT 405 MI...650 KM NNE OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 320 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...988 MB...29.18 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM HST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was
located near latitude 33.7 North, longitude 175.4 West.  Lala is
moving toward the northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h).  A slow
northwestward motion is forecast during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Gradual weakening is expected during the next several days.

Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles (240 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 988 mb (29.18 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------

$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 50
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Mon Aug 24 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 242041
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  50
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Mon Aug 24 2026
 
Lala has remained remarkably steady in organization over the past 
couple of days.  The storm continues to maintain moderate deep 
convection in banding features  with a ragged eye-like feature near 
the center.  The system is over sea surface temperatures of around 
25 deg C and there is apparently sufficient instability to allow 
the cyclone to maintain its convection for the time being.  Lala's 
current intensity is held at 55 kt in agreement with a Dvorak 
intensity estimate from PHFO Honolulu.  This is also a blend of 
objective estimates from UW-CIMSS.
 
The current motion estimate is around 320/4 kt, about the same as 
earlier this morning.  Lala is embedded in a broad cyclonic flow 
with fairly weak steering currents overall.  The system is still 
fairly well-removed from the faster deep-layer southwesterly flow 
at higher latitudes.  Therefore a continued slow motion is expected 
for the next few days, although a mid level ridge could build a bit 
to the northeast of the system and possibly impart a slightly 
faster forward speed.  The official forecast is a blend of the 
corrected dynamical model consensus and the Google DeepMind 
forecast.  This is quite similar to the previous NHC track.

Lala is expected to pass over gradually cooling ocean waters during 
the next several days.  This, along with a relatively dry low- to 
mid-level air mass, should result in slow weakening through the 
forecast period.  Simulated satellite imagery from the global 
models show the system losing most of its associated deep 
convection in around 72 hours so the official forecast indicates 
that Lala should transition into a post tropical cyclone near the 
time.

item.description:

BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Moke Advisory Number  18
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Mon Aug 24 2026
 
...FLASH FLOODING POSSIBLE FOR PORTIONS OF THE BIG ISLAND OF
HAWAII...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM HST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.7N 161.8W
ABOUT 515 MI...830 KM E OF JOHNSTON ISLAND
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 16 MPH...26 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM HST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Moke
was located near latitude 15.7 North, longitude 161.8 West.  The
depression is moving toward the west near 16 mph (26 km/h), and this
motion is expected to continue for the next day or two, taking the
system farther away from the Hawaiian Islands.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Weakening is expected, and Moke is forecast to degenerate to a
remnant low pressure area late today and dissipate on Tuesday.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Tropical Depression Moke can be found in the
Tropical Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header HFOTCDCP3 and WMO
header WTPA43 PHFO.
 
RAINFALL: Tropical Depression Moke is expected to produce isolated
additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches through Monday across
the Big Island and eastern Maui. This rainfall may produce areas of
flash flooding for portions of the Big Island, including
flood-prone and low-lying locations, as well as urban areas.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Depression Moke Forecast Discussion Number 18
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Mon Aug 24 2026 
000
WTPA43 PHFO 242032
TCDCP3
 
Tropical Depression Moke Discussion Number  18
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Mon Aug 24 2026

A large burst of convection has formed on the western side of Moke, 
with little convection elsewhere due to dry air.  Satellite 
intensity estimates are basically unchanged from earlier, so the 
initial wind speed remains 30 kt.  While many convective bursts can 
lead to intensification, some of these strong bursts can actually 
cause the system to weaken due to dry air entrainment and strong 
downbursts distorting the low-level circulation.  All of the 
models suggest that this is the last significant burst, and thus the 
system is likely to either open up in a trough or cease organized 
deep convection tonight.  Thus no changes were made to the intensity 
or dissipation forecast of Moke.

The depression continues moving just north of due west at about 14 
kt.  There are no changes to the forecast as a strong high pressure 
area steers the storm on the same general path for the next day or 
two.  Even though Moke is well southwest of the Hawaiian Islands, 
periods of heavy rain could still cause flash flooding across 
portions of the Big Island today.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Localized heavy rain associated with Tropical Depression Moke 
will continue over the Hawaiian Islands today.  This rainfall may 
produce areas of flash flooding for portions of the Big Island, 
including flood-prone and low-lying locations, as well as urban 
areas.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
